author: Hilary of Poitiers
translation: E. W. Watson (NPNF ser. 2 vol. 9, 1899), public domain
note: Hilary of Poitiers, the leading fourth-century Latin defender of the Nicene faith, grounds the Trinity in the baptismal command (Matthew 28:19): the Father from whom, the Son through whom, the Spirit who pervades all, each One. Verified verbatim 2026-08-24 (apologia-citations, web). 2026-11-18: re-verified word for word against the hosted 1899 text (/fathers/hilary-trinity-book-2.html, copy-checked against three archive.org scans) and extended by one sentence so it names the baptismal command it explains; translator corrected to E. W. Watson, who translated Books 1-7 (L. Pullan translated De Synodis, not this work); source_url moved from New Advent, which modernises the English, to a scan of the 1899 printing.
text: He bade them baptize in the Name of the Father, and of the Son, and of the Holy Ghost, that is with confession of the Creator and of the Only-begotten, and of the Gift. For God the Father is One, from Whom are all things; and our Lord Jesus Christ the Only-begotten, through Whom are all things, is One; and the Spirit, God's Gift to us, Who pervades all things, is also One.

author: Hilary of Poitiers
translation: E. W. Watson (NPNF ser. 2 vol. 9, 1899), public domain
note: The Son's eternal birth from the Father, against the Arian claim that he was made out of nothing. Verified word for word against the hosted 1899 text, 2026-11-18 (that text restores the printed 'begat', which CCEL's transcription modernises to 'begot').
text: He therefore, the Unbegotten, before time was begat a Son from Himself; not from any pre-existent matter, for all things are through the Son; not from nothing, for the Son is from the Father's self; not by way of childbirth, for in God there is neither change nor void.

author: Hilary of Poitiers
translation: S. C. Gayford (NPNF ser. 2 vol. 9, 1899), public domain
note: Hilary's answer to 'The Father is greater than I' (John 14:28): the Father is greater as Father, the Son is not less. The excerpt keeps both halves together on purpose, so it cannot be read as ranking the Son beneath the Father in nature. Verified word for word against the hosted 1899 text, 2026-11-18.
text: The Father, Who glorifies the Son, is greater: The Son, Who is glorified in the Father, is not less. How can He be less, when He is in the glory of God the Father? And how can the Father not be greater? The Father therefore is greater, because He is Father: but the Son, because He is Son, is not less.

author: Hilary of Poitiers
translation: S. C. Gayford (NPNF ser. 2 vol. 9, 1899), public domain
note: One person, God and man: the Son did not become two beings by taking humanity. Chosen from Book 10 deliberately away from 10.23, where Hilary says Christ felt suffering 'without its pain' (imprecise by later standards; the hosted page carries a note there). Verified word for word against the hosted 1899 text, 2026-11-18.
text: He was born also not to be at one time two separate beings, but that it might be made plain, that He Who was God before He was Man, now that He has taken humanity, is God and Man.

author: Hilary of Poitiers
translation: E. N. Bennett (NPNF ser. 2 vol. 9, 1899), public domain
note: Hilary's answer to the Arian slogan that 'there was a time when he was not': if the Father was always Father, the Son always was. Chosen (2026-11-18 review) over 12.31 ('So He was born and yet has always existed'), whose subject is never named, because the live AI sees only author, work, section, translation and text. Verified word for word against the hosted 1899 text, 2026-11-18.
text: For either He was not always a Father, unless there was always also a Son; or if He was always a Father, there was always also a Son; since whatever period of time is denied to the Son, to make His sonship non-eternal, just so much the Father lacks of having been always a Father

author: Hilary of Poitiers
translation: E. N. Bennett (NPNF ser. 2 vol. 9, 1899), public domain
note: Hilary's reserve, in his closing prayer: of the Spirit he will say only that he is God's Spirit, without prying further. The excerpt stops before the section's wording on the Spirit's origin ('from Thee and through Him'), which bears on the filioque question. Verified word for word against the hosted 1899 text, 2026-11-18.
text: I will not trespass beyond that which human intellect can know about Thy Holy Spirit, but simply declare that He is Thy Spirit.
